dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Propositional equality between two values of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires the real-valued measure of the absolute-value tail event to equal exactly the sum of the two one-sided real-valued measures.

dependency_coverage.name: GE.ge
dependency_coverage.meaning: The relation a >= b, defined by reversing the arguments of the ambient <= relation: b <= a.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes all three event predicates non-strict lower bounds: |S(ω)| >= t, S(ω) >= t, and -S(ω) >= t.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Addition supplied by a heterogeneous-addition instance; here it is instantiated with real numbers in every input and output position.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Combines the two real-valued one-sided event measures by ordinary real addition on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict-order relation supplied by an LT instance; here it is strict order on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses the threshold hypothesis 0 < t.

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function is measurable when the preimage of every measurable set in its codomain is measurable in its domain.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires S from Ω to the Borel real line to be measurable before the tail-measure equality is asserted.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: A measurable-space structure on a type, specifying which subsets are measurable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Equips the arbitrary sample type Ω with the measurable structure used by μ and by the measurability hypothesis on S.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: The proposition/typeclass condition that a measure is a probability measure, conventionally meaning that its total mass is one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Restricts μ to a probability measure and hence, in particular, makes all event measures finite.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: A measure on a type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the measure μ used to assign sizes to the three tail events.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real-valued measure of a set, defined by applying ENNReal.toReal to the measure's extended-nonnegative-real value on that set.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Places each of the three event measures in Real, so the asserted equality and addition are real-valued rather than directly statements in the extended nonnegative reals.

dependency_coverage.name: Neg.neg
dependency_coverage.meaning: Unary negation supplied by a Neg instance; here it is ordinary real negation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms -S(ω) in the second one-sided event, representing the lower tail of S as the upper tail of -S; it also participates in the definition of absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interprets a natural-number literal in a target type using its OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets the literal 0 in the hypothesis as the real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Is the codomain of S, the type of the threshold t, and the type of both sides of the equality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard addition operation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the right-hand side the ordinary real sum of the two real-valued event measures.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: The additive-group structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the additive inverse structure used by real absolute value, so |S(ω)| is built from S(ω) and -S(ω).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard non-strict order <= on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines the meanings of all three >= comparisons in the tail events.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard strict order < on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines the strict positivity condition 0 < t.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNeg
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard unary negation operation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the expression -S(ω) ordinary real negation in the second one-sided event and in the construction of real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The distinguished zero element of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the real zero appearing in the positive-threshold hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: The lattice structure on the real numbers, providing max and min with respect to their order.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the maximum operation used to define |S(ω)| as max(S(ω), -S(ω)).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.measurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Borel measurable-space structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the codomain measurable structure with respect to which S is required to be measurable.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: Builds the interpretation of the numeral 0 from a type's Zero instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Ensures that the numeral in 0 < t is exactly the standard real zero.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: Absolute value in a lattice-ordered additive group, defined here as max(a, -a).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the left-hand event the two-sided magnitude event {ω | |S(ω)| >= t}.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs homogeneous heterogeneous addition from an ordinary Add instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Selects ordinary real addition for the HAdd operation joining the two right-hand event measures.

dependency_coverage.name: setOf
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forms the set of all elements satisfying a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Turns each pointwise inequality in ω into the corresponding measurable-event subset of Ω whose μ.real value is taken.

binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
hypotheses: S is measurable from Ω to the Borel measurable space on ℝ.
The real threshold t is strictly positive: 0 < t.
The typeclass assumption says that μ is a probability measure.
conclusions: The real-valued measure of {ω ∈ Ω | |S(ω)| >= t} equals the real-valued measure of {ω ∈ Ω | S(ω) >= t} plus the real-valued measure of {ω ∈ Ω | -S(ω) >= t}.
mathematical_definitions: For every set A ⊆ Ω occurring here, its displayed real-valued measure is (μ(A)).toReal, the real conversion of the measure's extended-nonnegative-real value.
The event {-S >= t} is the lower-tail event {S <= -t} in ordinary real arithmetic.
Real absolute value is max(S(ω), -S(ω)), so when t > 0 the absolute-value tail is the union of the two one-sided events, which are disjoint.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every probability space (Ω, μ), every measurable real-valued function S on Ω, and every positive real number t, the probability of the two-sided tail event |S| >= t is exactly the sum of the probabilities of the upper-tail event S >= t and the reflected lower-tail event -S >= t (equivalently S <= -t), with probabilities represented by the real conversions of μ's values.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The claim is restricted to strictly positive thresholds t; it says nothing for t <= 0. Positivity is what prevents the two one-sided events from overlapping (at t = 0 they can overlap where S = 0).
The claim applies only to measures carrying an IsProbabilityMeasure instance and only to measurable real-valued functions S.

Each measure is compared after ENNReal.toReal conversion, rather than directly in the extended nonnegative reals. Under the probability-measure assumption all event measures are finite, so this conversion has the usual probability interpretation.
The statement uses non-strict tail events (>=), not strict tail events (>).
The proposition asserts only the numerical measure equality; it does not separately assert the underlying set union or disjointness identities.

If the required probability-measure instance or measurability proof is unavailable, the proposition has no applicable instantiation for that μ or S; these assumptions restrict applicability rather than strengthening the conclusion.
